This statement marked the first official confirmation of the detention and contained significantly more details than previous Turkish media reports. According to Gurek, Schueler, a US citizen for whom Interpol reportedly issued a red notice on charges of cryptocurrency fraud amounting to $1 billion in the US and Finland, was detained and placed under custody in Istanbul. Schueler, an American entrepreneur behind the HEX, Pulsechain, and Pulsex projects, was detained along with his wife. Three other men, reportedly his bodyguards, were subsequently detained. Investigators searched 15 properties in Besiktas, Uskudar, and Sariyer districts, acting in coordination with Turkish police intelligence units, financial crime investigators, and the country's National Intelligence Organization.cryptonews.ru41m agocryptonews.ru41m agoCrypto Scammer Loses $4.8 Million In Stolen Bitcoin To Another Group Of ThievesA cryptocurrency scammer reportedly lost roughly 60 BTC, worth about $4.8 million, after storing stolen proceeds in compromised hardware wallets. The funds came from an online employment scam that lured victims into depositing money with promises of earnings from simple online tasks. The operator moved the proceeds into wallets associated with Ledger hardware devices, which were then drained to an attacker-controlled address.

The case is tied to a wider supply-chain attack in which some hardware wallets sold through third-party resellers had been physically modified
